candidates.business_summary: We make small-interfering-RNA (siRNA) drugs that silence the gene behind a disease so the harmful protein is never made. Our lead drug, onvuzosiran, shuts down liver production of plasma kallikrein to prevent hereditary angioedema attacks with infrequent injections and is in Phase 3; behind it sit agazisiran for complement-driven kidney and eye disease and a Factor XI program for stroke prevention. We have no product revenue - we are funded by our IPO, private rounds and AbbVie, which paid $335M upfront in 2025 to license our platform for neurology, immunology and oncology targets and owes milestones and royalties on anything that works.

candidates.business_summary: We develop antibodies that kill the specific immune cells driving a runaway inflammatory response instead of suppressing the whole immune system. Our lead drug, ipsoprubart, targets SIRP proteins on overactive myeloid and T cells, and we are testing it first in secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis - a frequently fatal cytokine storm triggered by cancer, infection or immunotherapy that has no FDA-approved treatment - with a Phase 2/3 trial completing enrollment in the second half of 2027. We have no revenue; our IPO proceeds fund the program through an FDA filing, with runway guided into 2029.

candidates.business_summary: We make the optical transceivers that convert electrical signals to light and back inside AI data centers and telecom networks, plus the optical chips inside them and fiber-to-the-home terminals. About 70% of our revenue comes from datacom modules sold to cloud operators and network-equipment vendors, and we are in volume production of 800-gigabit and 1.6-terabit parts. We sell hardware by the unit on supply agreements; 2025 revenue was RMB 8.36B, up 64%, with RMB 873M of profit. Hisense Group is our controlling shareholder.
